back: A quantity with magnitude (size) only, e.g. mass, speed, energy.
A quantity with magnitude and direction, e.g. force, velocity, momentum.
Displacement, velocity, acceleration, force (also weight, momentum, field strength).
Distance, speed, time, mass (also energy, temperature).
The single vector with the same effect as two or more vectors acting together.

front: How do you add two vectors along the same line?
back: Add if they point the same way; subtract if opposite; the resultant points the way of the larger.

front: Resultant of two perpendicular vectors a and b?
back: Magnitude √(a² + b²); angle from tan θ = opposite ÷ adjacent.

front: What does 'nose to tail' mean in a vector diagram?
back: Draw the second arrow starting where the first ends; the resultant joins the tail of the first to the head of the second.

front: What is the difference between distance and displacement?
back: Distance is the path length (scalar); displacement is the straight-line change in position with direction (vector).
